title: release.sh dies silently on a GitHub blip and --resume refuses after the release commit
notes:
Seen cutting v2.43.0 (run 42395223367).

1. gh run watch failed with 'failed to get run: ... EOF' (a GitHub API blip) while the run was still going. The script then went into its failed-leg branch, whose gh run view also failed under set -eu inside the command substitution, so it exited with no 'Stopped:' line at all. The release was fine and still building. Fix: retry gh run watch on a transport error (as land.sh does with retries), and never let the failed-leg lookup exit silently; a watch that fails while the run is still in_progress goes back to watching.

2. scripts/release.sh --resume <run id> then refused with 'main is not origin/main. Pull or push until they match.', because the workflow's prepare job had pushed 'Release vX.Y.Z' to main. --resume is exactly the case where origin/main is ahead by that commit: fast-forward when local main is an ancestor of origin/main, refuse only on local commits or a dirty tree.

Tests for both decisions (a small module or the script's testable half), docs/workflow README scenarios and history.
